summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — PRX.AS +3%, REN.AS +3%, CCEP.L +3%, CPG.L +3%, BRBY.L +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (VNA.DE -7%, RHM.DE -5%, GLE.PA -5%, FRES.L -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: VNA.DE (-6.57%) — US strikes on Iran ended ceasefire, Brent crude spiked ~7.7% toward $80/bbl, driving bond yields up and hitting rate-sensitive German real estate sector-wide (LEG, TAG, Aroundtown also fell sharply). Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — VNA.DE is a large-cap German REIT/real-estate name, a sector this uk-eu universe likely excludes or under-weights; the move itself was a macro/rates-driven sector selloff with no idiosyncratic news, which single-name catalyst filters aren't designed to catch.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh company news; move tracks a rally in Tencent (its core holding) on HKEX, amplified by residual momentum from FY26 earnings beat and $5B buyback announced June 29.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Prosus is a mega-cap investment holding company (NAV pass-through vehicle for Tencent/Naspers stakes), not a standard operating-company sector name, so cap/sector filters likely exclude holding-company structures entirely.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an investment-holding-company category to the uk-eu universe with a rule that gates entry on the underlying asset's move (e.g., Tencent HKEX gap ≥3%) rather than PRX's own technicals.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news catalyst; likely drift from RELX's ongoing £100m buyback tranche (1-21 Jul, part of £2.25bn 2026 plan) and pre-earnings positioning ahead of Jul 23 results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — REN.AS is the Euronext Amsterdam secondary listing of RELX PLC, whose primary listing is LSE:REL.L; universe construction likely keys off primary-exchange tickers only, so this dual-listing symbol is never enumerated.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend the universe builder to map known dual-listed secondary tickers (e.g., REN.AS -> REL.L) to the same underlying entity so existing signals/positions on the primary listing also register coverage on the secondary venue.

top_movers.catalyst: Wells Fargo raised CCEP PT to $115 (Jul 8) and Deutsche Bank to 8480p (Jul 2); active €500mn buyback tranche plus defensive-staples rotation amid Iran-ceasefire risk-off supported the move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CCEP is a large-cap (~$47B) UK/EU consumer-staples bottler, dual-listed LSE/Nasdaq; likely excluded by sector (staples/defensive) or region-tagging confusion from its US ADR listing, not a technical filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE100 large-cap consumer-staples names (mkt cap >$30B) to the uk-eu universe, and fix region-tagging so LSE-primary/Nasdaq-dual-listed tickers like CCEP aren't miscategorized as US-only.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh company news on 2026-07-09 (last RNS was the May 11 H1 beat/guidance raise); move looks like continued re-rating drift ahead of the July 21 Q3 update, aided by broad FTSE 100 strength.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CPG.L is a mega-cap FTSE 100 contract-catering/support-services name, a defensive/staples sector the bot's uk-eu momentum & news-reactive strategies don't cover; also redenominated its LSE quote from GBp to USD on 2026-04-01, which likely breaks GBP-keyed universe/eligibility fi
top_movers.suggestion: Audit the uk-eu universe builder for a GBP-currency assumption on LSE listings and whitelist USD-quoted LSE names like CPG.L explicitly, since a silent currency-redenomination can drop a FTSE 100 constituent from coverage without any alert.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news catalyst found — stock has been depressed near 52-week lows on a revenue turnaround story, with the AGM not until 2026-07-15; move looks like a technical/short-covering bounce.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BRBY.L is a UK large-cap luxury/consumer-discretionary name currently in a documented revenue-decline turnaround story, a profile uk-eu strategies likely exclude via a sector or trend-quality filter (negative revenue growth, near 52-week lows) rather than a liquidity/cap cutoff.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a controlled carve-out to the uk-eu universe for FTSE 100 constituents currently excluded on trend-quality grounds, gated by a mean-reversion signal (e.g., >2% bounce off a 20-day low on >1.2x avg volume) rather than a blanket sector exclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: Brent crude spiked ~5% (to ~$79/bbl) as US-Iran tensions escalated (US revoked Iran crude waiver, Iran struck US bases in Bahrain/Kuwait), lifting UK oil majors sector-wide.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — BP.L is a large-cap FTSE 100 UK oil major, a geography/sector (UK-listed integrated energy) the bot's tradable universe doesn't cover, so no filter ever saw it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK large-cap energy bucket (e.g. FTSE 100 oil & gas majors) to the uk-eu universe with a geopolitical-event gate keyed off Brent/WTI intraday % move, so oil-sensitive names become tradable on sector-wide crude spikes.

top_movers.catalyst: US strikes on Iran ended ceasefire, Brent crude spiked ~7.7% toward $80/bbl, driving bond yields up and hitting rate-sensitive German real estate sector-wide (LEG, TAG, Aroundtown also fell sharply).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — VNA.DE is a large-cap German REIT/real-estate name, a sector this uk-eu universe likely excludes or under-weights; the move itself was a macro/rates-driven sector selloff with no idiosyncratic news, which single-name catalyst filters aren't designed to catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rate-sensitive EU real-estate/REIT basket (VNA, LEG, TAG, AT1) gated on a macro trigger (Brent ≥5% intraday move or Bund 10Y yield spike ≥10bp) instead of requiring per-name news catalysts.

top_movers.catalyst: Broker downgrade cycle continues: MWB Research cut RHM.DE to Sell (PT €1,450) on fears NATO budgets are pivoting to air-defense/drones, adding to Berenberg/JPMorgan cuts after Germany scrapped the F126 frigate deal in late June.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RHM.DE is a DAX-listed defense/industrial mega-cap, a sector likely excluded from the uk-eu universe via an ESG/arms-sector screen or simply never added despite its size and liquidity.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/XETRA defense-adjacent names (RHM.DE, etc.) to the uk-eu universe watchlist with an explicit ESG-exclusion flag, so future misses are a documented policy choice rather than a silent coverage gap.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-name news: sector-wide French bank selloff as OAT-Bund spread widened on budget/political uncertainty, compounded by oil-driven bond yield spikes from Middle East/Iran tensions.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLE.PA (CAC40 bank) isn't in the uk-eu tradable list, so this was a macro/rates-driven sector move with no strategy positioned to react regardless of signal quality.
top_movers.suggestion: Add major CAC40 banks (GLE.PA, BNP.PA, ACA.PA) to the uk-eu universe with a rates-sensitivity tag so sector-wide moves tied to OAT-Bund spread widening become tradable, not just single-name catalysts.

top_movers.catalyst: Broker price-target cuts (Barclays to 3200p from 3775p, Berenberg also trimmed) amid a weak week for silver (dollar strength, Mideast-driven risk-off) hit precious-metals miners broadly.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — FRES.L is a UK-listed (LSE) primary-listing precious-metals miner, a sector/geography the bot's equity universes likely exclude (commodity-linked mining names, non-US primary listings).
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK/LSE precious-metals-miner sleeve (or a silver-proxy equity list) to the universe so broker-downgrade/commodity-driven gappers like FRES.L are visible to a news-reactive or sector-momentum strategy.
